questions.stem: A deploy service keeps its listeners in an ArrayList and publishes with `for (DeployListener l : listeners) l.onDeploy(d);`. The listeners, in order, are `auditLog`, `firstDeployBanner` and `pager`. `firstDeployBanner` shows a banner for the first deploy of the day and then calls `listeners.remove(this)` from inside `onDeploy`. What happens on the first deploy of the day?

options.text: publish throws ConcurrentModificationException before pager is reached, since the list changed while the loop was walking it
options.says: with the leaver second of three, the list shrinks to the iterator's position, hasNext() reports the end, and nothing throws

options.text: publish throws ConcurrentModificationException after pager is called, since the loop checks for changes only once it has finished
options.says: nothing throws in this position, and the listener after the leaver is never called, as in the page's coupon-second run

options.text: Nothing is thrown and pager gets the deploy, since the removal only takes effect once the loop is over
options.says: an ArrayList removal takes effect at once; only a copy-on-write list or a copy lets the dispatch walk the old list

options.text: Nothing is thrown and pager misses the deploy, since the loop takes the shorter list to mean it is done
options.says: the page's coupon-second run: no exception, and the listener after the one that left silently misses the event

origin.section: A Listener That Unsubscribes During a Dispatch Changes the List Being Walked

questions.stem: A `ThemePanel` calls `themes.addListener(this::repaint)` in `show()` and `themes.removeListener(this::repaint)` in `hide()`. `ThemeService` keeps its listeners in a CopyOnWriteArrayList and removes with `List.remove`. A user shows and hides the panel 30 times on the same `ThemePanel` object. How many listeners does `ThemeService` hold afterwards?

options.text: 0, since the this::repaint in hide() names the same method on the same object as the one in show() and so compares equal
options.says: a method reference doesn't override equals; each evaluation of this::repaint was a new object, and the run printed a.equals(b) false

options.text: 1, since the copy-on-write list ignores the this::repaint in show() when it already holds one for that panel
options.says: each this::repaint is a new object not equal to the one already registered, so nothing makes the list treat it as a duplicate

options.text: 30, since the this::repaint in hide() is a new object each time and matches no listener in the list
options.says: the page's dashboard run: remove(this::onOrder) left the listener in place; 30 shows add 30 listeners and remove none

options.text: 30, since the this::repaint in hide() is removed only from the copy that the next write to the list replaces
options.says: removal from a CopyOnWriteArrayList takes effect at once; the miss is that the argument is a different object

origin.section: A Listener Is Removed by the Reference It Was Added With, and a Second Lambda Is Another Object

questions.stem: A chat client's `ConversationView` holds the conversation's last 5,000 messages. Its constructor calls `bus.subscribe(this::onMessage)` on a `MessageBus` that lives as long as the application. Its `close()` sets a `closed` field, and `onMessage` returns at once when `closed` is true; nothing unsubscribes. After a user opens and closes 400 conversations, what does the heap hold?

options.text: All 400 views and their messages, since the bus's list holds each method reference and each reference holds its view
options.says: the report-screen run: 200 closed screens stayed reachable through the subject's list, 202 MB; the flag only stops the work

options.text: All 400 method references but none of the views, since a method reference keeps the method and not the object it was taken from
options.says: this::onMessage captures this, so the list keeps every view and everything it holds

options.text: Only the open views, since the closed flag lets the bus drop a view that no longer handles messages
options.says: the bus never looks at the view's field; only a removal takes the entry out of the list

options.text: Only the open views, since nothing in the user interface refers to a closed view once it is gone from the screen
options.says: the bus's list still refers to it, and that is enough to keep it reachable

origin.section: The Subject Keeps Every Listener, and Everything It Captures, Until It Is Removed

questions.stem: A telemetry agent publishes 500 CPU samples a second through a `SubmissionPublisher` with a buffer of 32. Its one subscriber writes each sample to a remote store, asks for one at a time, and manages 50 a second. The agent publishes with `offer(sample, (sub, s) -> false)`. What happens over the next minute?

options.text: The agent keeps its pace and most samples are lost, since the handler returning false tells offer to discard what doesn't fit
options.says: the page's offer run: 100 offered in 4 ms, 91 dropped, 9 handled; returning false means drop

options.text: The agent keeps its pace and every sample is stored, since the handler returning false lets the publisher grow the buffer instead
options.says: the buffer is bounded; returning false means drop, and bounding the buffer is what Flow adds over a queue to another thread

options.text: The agent slows to the subscriber's pace and every sample is stored, since offer waits for room and never calls the handler
options.says: that is submit; offer returns at once and hands the item to the drop handler

options.text: The agent slows to the subscriber's pace and samples are lost, since the handler returning false cancels the subscriber once it is full
options.says: returning false drops the item; the publisher cancels a subscriber whose method throws, not a slow one

origin.section: When a Subscriber Can't Keep Up, a Flow Publisher Makes the Producer Wait or Drop
